items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: I had a friend of mine called Herman the German.

ctx.x: Then, every summer we take off and go down through Texas and Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee. We play all over the South. I don't think there's a place in the South where I ain't never been. I made so many stops...one-nighters...call me "One-Nighters Joe." 'Course, Ray Charles, Bobby Blue Bland, B.B. King an' all them fellows, they were doin' the same thing. That's all we played was one-nighters. We didn't play too many nightclubs. When we did, we just stayed three days... weekends...and we had a lot of fun…

So we talkin' about whenever anybody would have a good night ...made some extra money...we'd all come out and have a good time the next day. I had a friend of mine called Herman the German. I met him down in Houston, Texas. I was workin' at a place called the Peacock Nightclub. Don Roby (?) run it, and, uh...we, uh, used to play there sometimes a month in the nightclub, and so I run into Herman the German

items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: He used to be a good, little white fellow. He come by a-a-a-a-a-l-lll... every month... Do your dance, Cous.

ctx.x: So the cat...when he come back next month to pay off, the cats say, "You owe us thirty dollars." Say, "No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. I don't owe you no thirty dollars. Owe you twenty-one dollars." Say, "Whaddya mean? I sold you so many half-pints..." "Jus' a minute." He go in the bathroom, and "Shit, look, I mark 'em down." And couldn't get by that. "I mark 'em down...how many half-pints I got."

One time he got drunk...we looked for him for two days. He went in the basement...went down in the basement where they kept the coal at...was down there asleep. So I had to go down in the basement one day and find him down there asleep...set layin' on the floor asleep. So I got him up, took him upstairs, washed his face and everything, got him back straight. He went right back to drinkin'. I never will forget him. He used to be a good, little white fellow. He come by a-a-a-a-a-l-lll... every month. He didn't miss…
